decisive_spans.text: He had an upper respiratory illness three weeks earlier
On hospital day 4, he was unable to walk unassisted, had complete flaccid paralysis of the right arm, left arm strength 3/5, and areflexia throughout all extremities.

response.rationale: The patient presents with acute progressive limb weakness and areflexia following a recent upper respiratory illness, which are classic features of Guillain-Barré Syndrome. D1 (Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy) is a very close synonym and shares many features, but D3 is a more common and encompassing term for this presentation. D4 (Botulism) is contradicted by a negative serum assay for botulinum toxin. D9 (Spinal Cord Infarction) is contradicted by unremarkable cervical-spine imaging.
